items.method: Cross-read cash-market breadth (share of constituents positive versus the 60% broad-participation threshold) against the single-name options tape (call-versus-put premium, call fraction and the strike and days-to-expiry of the heaviest same-session prints), the dealer-positioning corridor (negative dealer gamma, flip, put and call walls, front expected move, range-break-watch playbook) and the intraday auction state, then judge whether a broad breadth reading meeting a bullish call tape now sits above a short-gamma dealer structure that would amplify a downside break, and anchor a direction-correct invalidation below the benchmark at the put-wall loss that would falsify the constructive lean.
items.note: The genuinely new configuration this window is that breadth and the single-name options tape both point the same constructive way while the dealer structure remains negative gamma, so the internal signal and the flow signal reinforce upside even as the mechanical damping that cushions calmer windows is absent. Market-heatmap breadth is 67% of 134 constituents positive, a wide 7-point cushion over the 60% broad-participation threshold. Single-name option premium is outright call-heavy: a 0.6926 call fraction, $2.572B of call premium against $1.142B of put premium across 12 tickers, with 1707 contracts clearing the $250k bar inside 30 days (485 of 16610 considered). The heaviest near-dated prints are an upside chase — a QQQ 709 call at $54.4M on 137x its open interest zero days out and a TSLA 355 call at $53.8M on 69x open interest zero days out — though a SPY 765 put at $27.6M on 189.9x open interest zero days out shows real same-strike hedging at spot. That flow lands on a negative dealer-gamma structure: SPY reads negative gamma with the flip near 767.73, put wall 760 and call wall 765 inside a plus-or-minus 8.93 front expected move, signed net GEX about -3.73B, and the gamma playbook is range-break-watch with a patient, same-session-fade hold. The most recent intraday auction is a Trend day · up under Algo-controlled control (VWAP 764.72, +0.10% gap, 79 bars). With breadth broad, flow bullish and the benchmark carried near 765.16 just beneath the 767.73 flip, the read leans constructive but fragile: the call demand and broad participation lean higher, yet spot sitting under the flip in negative gamma means a break lower would be amplified, not cushioned. The confirming trigger for the constructive case is the benchmark reclaiming the 767.73 flip to pull dealers back toward positive gamma while breadth holds above 60%; the constructive lean is invalidated on a daily close below ~760.00 on SPY, which loses the 760 put wall, would leave dealers selling into weakness in negative gamma and would show the call premium was chasing a top rather than leading a durable advance.
items.title: Breadth is broad at 67% of 134 constituents while the single-name option tape is outright call-heavy at a 0.6926 call fraction ($2.572B calls vs $1.142B puts across 12 names, 1707 contracts clearing the $250k bar) — the heaviest prints a QQQ 709 call at $54.4M on 137x open interest and a TSLA 355 call at $53.8M zero days out against a SPY 765 put hedge at $27.6M — yet SPY dealers remain negative gamma with the flip at 767.73 and walls 760/765 inside a plus-or-minus 8.93 expected move and spot at 764.62 sitting below the flip, so the constructive internals sit over an amplifying rather than damping dealer structure while the intraday auction reads Trend day · up at VWAP 764.72

items.method: Cross-read the firming US internals (breadth wide above the participation line, call-heavy single-name premium, an up-trend intraday auction) against where leadership is actually being scored — the global-rotation composite (Singapore far ahead of the US-heavy ACWI, with Taiwan, Brazil, Canada and Australia next) and the real-assets 0-100 composite (crypto and broad commodities leading, gold weak and rate-shadowed, silver weaker, oil firmer) — to test whether risk appetite still concentrates offshore and in real assets while the domestic tape confirms, then, finding the leadership cluster resolves to relative-strength scores and composite rankings rather than any single committed-universe price level, withhold a tactical call rather than publish one that cannot be scored.
items.note: The second cross-model pattern this window is that the leadership scores keep pointing offshore and into real assets even as US internals stay constructive, so the migration remains a where-is-the-bid observation rather than a confirmation of index direction. The US picture is firm: market-heatmap breadth is wide at 67% of 134 constituents, single-name option premium is call-heavy at a 0.6926 call fraction ($2.572B calls versus $1.142B puts), and the intraday auction is a Trend day · up under Algo-controlled control at VWAP 764.72. Against that, global rotation ranks EWS (Singapore) first at 93.6/100 versus the US-heavy ACWI, with EWT (Taiwan) 74.5, EWZ (Brazil) 69.9, EWC (Canada) 69, EWA (Australia) 68.3 and EWU (United Kingdom) 66.1 ahead of a middling US read. Real assets are led by crypto and broad commodities — ETH-USD 75.1, PDBC 73.5 (six-month momentum +22.49%), DBC 73.3 (+22.15%), agriculture DBA 72.5, bitcoin (BTC-USD) 67.9 and IBIT 66.6 — while oil (USO) 64.2 is a firmer uptrend on a flat +0.21% three-month but a strong +54.16% six-month pulse, and the monetary metals stay weak: gold (GLD) reads 40 mixed with six-month momentum of -14.63%, and silver (SLV) 19 stays weak and mixed at -21.6%. Offshore-equity and speculative real-asset leadership with a weak, rate-shadowed gold and weaker silver, set against a US sector rotation that rotates into technology (XLK Improving, accel +1.36) with healthcare the named but weakening leader (XLV, accel -2.3) as energy rolls over (XLE Weakening, accel -2.89), is a where-is-the-bid observation, not a scoreable trade: the cluster resolves to relative-strength states and 0-100 composite scores, none of which is a single committed-universe instrument with a direction-correct price trigger this window, so a tactical call is withheld rather than published with only a working side. Watch whether US breadth holds above the 60% participation line to close the gap with the offshore and real-asset leadership, or whether the composite reads roll domestic leadership lower; until an instrument-level price trigger is in view, the cluster is carried as counter-weight context to the index-level constructive lean, not as its own call.
items.title: Leadership still sits offshore and in speculative real assets while US internals stay firm — global rotation ranks Singapore (EWS 93.6), Taiwan (EWT 74.5), Brazil (EWZ 69.9), Canada (EWC 69) and Australia (EWA 68.3) ahead of the US-heavy ACWI, and real assets are led by crypto and broad commodities (ETH-USD 75.1, PDBC 73.5, DBC 73.3, DBA 72.5, BTC-USD 67.9, IBIT 66.6) with oil (USO 64.2) firmer, gold (GLD 40, six-month momentum -14.63%) weak and rate-shadowed and silver (SLV 19, -21.6%) weaker, a cross-model migration that resolves to no single committed-universe price level
